sections.html:
Indianola is the seat of Warren County, a south central Iowa county that forms part of the Des Moines metro. It borders Polk to the north, Marion to the east, Lucas to the southeast, Clarke to the southwest and Madison to the west. Urban areas hold 52.9 percent of residents, and 80.2 percent of occupied housing units are lived in by their owners.

The 2020 count was 52,403 and the 2025 estimate is 57,331, after growth of 13.4 percent over the prior decade. Indianola had 15,833 people in 2020, Norwalk 12,799 and Carlisle 4,160. Slices of Des Moines and West Des Moines fall inside the county, so a house with a Des Moines or West Des Moines address may still be taxed here. Look up the parcel.

Indianola is a college and balloon town about 19 miles south of downtown Des Moines, home to Simpson College and the National Balloon Classic each summer. Iowa Highway 92 crosses the city and meets US 65 and 69 southeast of downtown. Indianola's school district has four elementary schools, a middle school and a high school.

Rental owners in Indianola must register and pass an inspection every two years. If you are selling a rented house, check its certificate with Code Enforcement at 515-962-5275.

Norwalk grew through annexations and new subdivisions at the edge of the metro, from 6,884 people in 2000 to 12,799 in 2020, with an estimated 15,004 in 2025. Michael Foods is building an $85 million distribution center there. Carlisle sits between the North and Middle rivers and grew from 3,497 residents in 2000 to 4,160 in 2020. Fast-growing towns mean a lot of newer houses, so a seller of an older home competes with recent builds. Gather the deed, the latest tax statement, mortgage payoff details and any rental certificate before you call us, so the title work moves quickly.

Most county offices work out of the Administration Building, 301 N. Buxton Street, Indianola. The Warren County Justice Center opened in summer 2022.

  • Treasurer: Suite 102, 515-690-9240, propertytax@warrencountyia.org. It keeps weekday hours of 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and appointments are the norm, so phone first.
  • Assessor: Suite 108, 515-690-9170, assessor@warrencountyia.org.
  • Recorder: Suite 109, 515-690-9110, recorder@warrencountyia.org. The county site links the Declaration of Value form and a transfer tax calculator.

You can also pay online at iowatreasurers.org, where Warren County is county ID 91.

Assessed value equals 100 percent of fair market value on January 1, ahead of any state rollback, and real property is revalued on a two-year cycle.

  • An informal review with the assessor is open April 2 through April 25.
  • A written Board of Review protest is open April 2 through April 30, limited to the grounds in Iowa Code 441.37.
  • In odd-numbered equalization years, notices are due by October 8. Protests of equalization changes are taken October 9 through October 31, and the Board sits October 10 through November 15.

Neither collecting tax nor setting rates is the assessor's job: the treasurer collects, and each taxing body sets its levy after a public hearing. The county site links forms for the homestead credit, military exemption, disabled veteran credit and family farm.

The fiscal 2027 county levy is 5.64659 per $1,000 of taxable value for urban property and 8.38166 for rural property, down 3.36 and 2.80 percent from fiscal 2026. The residential rollback, which turns assessed value into taxable value, is 44.5345 percent against 47.4316 percent the year before. Residential property makes up 87 percent of assessed value and 80 percent of taxable value in the county.

sections.h2: Due dates and what happens at closing
sections.html:
Payments are split in two, with September 1 and March 1 as the due dates. Once the grace date passes, 1.5 percent interest is added at the start of each month.

A typical sale prorates the year's taxes, crediting the buyer for the seller's share on the settlement statement. Past-due city utility or service bills can be certified to the treasurer and collected like taxes, which is why title companies search for them.

Iowa Code 428A.3 makes the seller owe the real estate transfer tax, 80 cents per $500 past the first $500. Recording waits until that tax is paid.

An online tax sale takes place every June on the GovEase platform, with the delinquent list printed in The Carlisle Citizen first.

  • Owners hear about the sale within 15 days.
  • To redeem, you pay the sale amount plus 2 percent a month, and a partial month is billed as a full one.
  • The 90-day redemption notice can go out after 1 year and 9 months on a regular sale, or 9 months on a public bidder sale.
  • Fees include $20 for a certificate and $25 for a treasurer's deed.

If your parcel was already sold, ask the treasurer for the redemption figure before you set a closing.

sections.h2: A seller's calendar through the tax year
sections.html:
Early in the year the assessment notice arrives, and April is the window to ask about it. Through the summer, the county sets levies after hearings. September 1 brings the first payment, and March 1 the second, so a sale in the spring or fall usually involves a proration on the settlement statement.

If you are thinking about selling, call the assessor in April if the value looks wrong, and call the treasurer in August or February if you are unsure what is owed. Waiting past a due date adds interest each month, and an unpaid parcel can end up in the June tax sale, which complicates any closing.

Our offers cover Warren County houses in any condition, including ones with delinquent taxes, a tax sale certificate or an unpaid utility lien. Share the address and the tax statement and a written offer follows, giving you a figure to compare with the redemption amount.

The title company settles taxes, redemption amounts and liens out of the sale money and sends you the balance. Get a written payoff from the treasurer before choosing a date, and if the house is rented, ask the city about the rental certificate.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Warren County, Iowa?
faqs.a: Indianola, with 15,833 residents in 2020. The county administration offices are at 301 N. Buxton Street.

faqs.q: How do I protest a Warren County assessment?
faqs.a: Two routes: an informal review with the assessor from April 2 to April 25, or a written Board of Review protest from April 2 to April 30 on the grounds in Iowa Code 441.37.

faqs.q: Which Warren County school district has the highest levy?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2027, Carlisle at 17.22926 per $1,000, followed by Indianola at 17.11308. Pleasantville is lowest at 14.19761.

faqs.q: How is the residential rollback changing in Warren County?
faqs.a: It dropped to 44.5345 percent for fiscal 2027 from 47.4316 percent in fiscal 2026, so a smaller share of assessed value is taxed.

faqs.q: What does it cost to redeem a Warren County tax sale parcel?
faqs.a: The sale amount, 2 percent per month with partial months counted in full, and a $20 certificate fee. The treasurer at 515-690-9240 can give the exact payoff.
